data.outcome_summary: The OECD Survey of Adult Skills 2023 country note for Poland reports adults’ proficiency in three domains—literacy, numeracy, and adaptive problem solving—based on a digital, tablet-based assessment administered in 2022-23 to adults aged 16-65. Poland’s mean performance is below the OECD average in all three domains (literacy: 236; numeracy: 239; adaptive problem solving: 226 on 500-point scales). The note reports proficiency-level distributions, including high shares at Level 1 or below (literacy: 39%; numeracy: 38%; adaptive problem solving: 48%) and smaller shares at the top levels (e.g., literacy Levels 4-5: 3%). It also documents changes over time versus 2011-12, with declines in literacy and numeracy and shifts toward lower proficiency levels. A key methodological caveat is that Poland had data-quality issues for a high share of respondents with unusual response patterns, so results require greater caution than for other participants.
